body.stem: You have a platform team that must be able to add, rename, move and remove management groups beneath the Contoso IT scope. You need this team to reshape the hierarchy without letting it change who has access or which policies are assigned. Which built-in Azure role should you assign at the Contoso IT management group?

options.text: Management Group Contributor
Owner
Contributor
Management Group Reader

explanation.correct: The documented chart of supported actions on a management group shows Management Group Contributor as the only built-in role that supports create, rename, move and delete while offering neither assign access nor assign policy. That is exactly the delegated change-making task without access or policy rights. (Note that moving items still requires the extra permissions listed for move operations.)

perChoice.b: Owner supports every action in the chart, including assign access and assign policy, so it hands the team far more than the reshaping task requires and lets it change governance conditions.
perChoice.c: Contributor supports create, rename, move, delete and assign access. It would let the team change who has access, which is explicitly outside what the team should be allowed to do.
perChoice.d: Management Group Reader only supports the read action on the management group scope, so the team could not create, rename, move or delete management groups.

body.stem: You created a custom role at the contoso-sandbox management group and assigned that role on the two subscriptions underneath it. Someone tried to place sub-sandbox-1 under contoso-corp, and the request was rejected with an error about breaking the link between the role definition and the assignment. What change lets sub-sandbox-1 succeed?

rows: Set sub-sandbox-1 as a child of /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/contoso-corp

options.text: Remove the role assignment from the subscription, then move the subscription under the new parent.
Remove the Owner role assignment on the target management group, then retry the request.
Move the management group that holds the role definition so it remains the parent of both subscriptions in the new branch.
Grant Reader on the target management group, then retry the request.

explanation.correct: This is the documented scenario where a subscription that carries a role assignment is moved outside the branch of the management group used in the custom role definition's assignable scope. The service rejects the move because the assignment can no longer reach the definition, and the documented fix is to remove the role assignment from the subscription before moving it to its new parent.

perChoice.b: The rejection is not caused by access permissions on the destination scope, so deleting an Owner role assignment there leaves the definition and the subscription assignment just as disconnected as before.
perChoice.c: Relocating the management group that holds the definition does not help the subscription that is being moved: its assignment would still point to a role definition it can no longer reach from its branch. The documented fixes concern the subscription's assignment or the definition's assignable scope.
perChoice.d: A built-in read-only role on the destination scope has no bearing on the relationship between a custom role definition and a subscription-level assignment, so the move keeps failing.

body.stem: You need sub-prod-01 to become a child of contoso-finance, and the access you hold across the hierarchy is listed below. Can you perform that change?

rows: Role assignment created on that scope
contoso-finance (scope you want sub-prod-01 to move under)
Role assignment created on that scope

options.text: Yes. Because the Owner role on sub-prod-01 was assigned on the subscription rather than inherited, your Contributor role on contoso-finance is enough for the destination.
No. The Owner role on sub-prod-01 is inherited from contoso-sales, so you need an Owner role assigned on contoso-finance before the subscription can move there.
No. contoso-sales is the top scope of the directory, so no permission checks apply when anything leaves it.
Yes. A Contributor role on contoso-finance grants ownership of every subscription placed under it.

explanation.correct: The documentation treats the two cases differently. When the Owner role is assigned on the subscription rather than inherited from its parent management group, you can move it to any management group where you hold the Contributor role, which is exactly your situation. The per-layer permissions for a move are met as well: Owner on the subscription supplies the management group and subscription write plus role assignment permissions required on the child, Contributor on the target management group supplies management group write there, and Owner on the current parent supplies it for the current parent.

perChoice.b: This describes the inherited case, which isn't your situation: the exhibit shows the Owner assignment was created on the subscription. If ownership were inherited from contoso-sales, you could only move the subscription to a management group where you also had Owner, because moving to a scope where you hold just Contributor would cost you ownership.
perChoice.c: The exception for the top scope only removes the permission requirements for that scope as target or existing parent; it doesn't waive the permissions needed on the child subscription and on the new parent, and it doesn't give the new parent any authority over the subscription.
perChoice.d: Contributor on a management group does not confer ownership of the subscriptions placed under it. Ownership only decides whether an inherited Owner role survives the move.

body.stem: A designer produced the following nesting for a governance rollout. Which service limit does this plan exceed?

options.text: The depth of the hierarchy: a management group tree can be six management group levels deep, not counting the top level or the subscription level.
The number of management groups a single directory can hold, which is 10,000.
The number of parent management groups each management group may have, which is one.
The number of Microsoft Entra tenants the subscriptions can come from, since one management group requires subscriptions that trust the same tenant.

explanation.correct: The documented ceiling is that a management group tree supports up to six levels of depth, and that count deliberately excludes the root level and the subscription level. The plan stacks seven management groups between the top scope and the subscriptions, so it sits one beyond what the service allows and the deepest group must be flattened.

perChoice.b: 10,000 is the documented cap on how many management groups one directory can contain. The plan uses only a handful of groups, so the count is not what it exceeds.
perChoice.c: One parent per management group is the documented rule about parentage, not a restriction on how deeply groups may be nested. The plan assigns a single parent to each group, so that rule isn't violated.
perChoice.d: The same-tenant rule is a constraint on which subscriptions may sit under one management group. The plan says nothing about tenants, so it isn't the limit being exceeded.

body.stem: You have Reader on contoso-corp only, as listed below. You need to add a management group beneath contoso-sandbox. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: Any Microsoft Entra ID user in the tenant can create a management group when hierarchy protection isn't enabled, and the creator receives an Owner role assignment on it.
Your account must first be granted a Contributor role assignment on the contoso-sandbox management group from an Owner there.
Your account must first be granted the User Access Administrator role on the management group at the top of the hierarchy.
Your account must wait for the first management group created in the directory to finish provisioning, which can take about 15 minutes.

explanation.correct: The quickstart states that any Microsoft Entra ID user in the tenant can create a management group without management group write permission assigned to them, as long as hierarchy protection isn't enabled, and that the creator is given an Owner role assignment on the group they just made. With hierarchy protection off, your account can create the group under contoso-sandbox straight away.

perChoice.b: The service intentionally avoids requiring a management group write permission for this task so that role assignments don't have to exist at the root; a Contributor assignment on contoso-sandbox isn't a prerequisite.
perChoice.c: Gaining access at the top of the hierarchy through the User Access Administrator role is about managing the hierarchy directory-wide, not a precondition for adding a group underneath an existing one.
perChoice.d: The roughly 15-minute delay applies to the very first management group created in a directory while the service is set up. The exhibit shows the hierarchy already exists, and even during that initial setup the service lets users in the tenant create a management group.

body.stem: A management group in your directory was relabelled by the team that founded it, and its name in the Azure portal no longer matches the company standard. You need the portal label changed to 'Corporate Landing Zones' while the identifier stays exactly as it is so that automation scripts and existing role assignments keep working. Which command should you run?

options.text: Update-AzManagementGroup -GroupId 'contoso-landing-zones' -DisplayName 'Corporate Landing Zones'
New-AzManagementGroup -GroupId 'contoso-landing-zones' -DisplayName 'Corporate Landing Zones'
Update-AzManagementGroup -GroupId 'Landing Zones (old)' -DisplayName 'Corporate Landing Zones'
Remove-AzManagementGroup -GroupId 'contoso-landing-zones'

explanation.correct: Update-AzManagementGroup updates an existing management group, and -DisplayName changes only the label shown in the Azure portal. The identifier that scripts and role assignments depend on is supplied through -GroupId, which takes the directory-unique management group ID (for example Update-AzManagementGroup -GroupId 'ContosoIt' -DisplayName 'Contoso Group'). Because that identifier can't be edited after creation, changing the display name is the only way to relabel the container without disturbing references, and the children stay attached to the same group.

perChoice.b: New-AzManagementGroup creates a brand-new container rather than relabelling an existing one. Creation requires a new unique identifier, and the identifier of an existing group can't be reused or changed, so this neither relabels contoso-landing-zones nor preserves its children.
perChoice.c: -GroupId takes the directory-unique identifier of the management group, not the label shown in the portal. Passing 'Landing Zones (old)' means the command has no group to resolve, so the update never reaches the intended management group.
perChoice.d: Remove-AzManagementGroup deletes the management group instead of renaming it. Deletion requires that no child management groups or subscriptions remain underneath, and this group still holds sub-prod-eu and sub-prod-us, so it can't be used to change the label.

body.stem: The sandbox environment has been retired and contoso-sandbox must no longer appear in the hierarchy, while the subscriptions and management group sitting beneath it have to keep running under contoso-corp. Which action should be taken?

options.text: Move the child management group and the subscriptions under it to a different parent management group, and delete contoso-sandbox with write permission on that group
Delete contoso-sandbox immediately with Contributor permission, and let the subscriptions and the child management group underneath be cleaned up at the same time
Move contoso-sandbox itself under a different parent management group and leave its contents in place, so it no longer appears beneath contoso-corp
Ask a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator to remove contoso-sandbox and its subscriptions from the tenant root group, and then let the hierarchy settle

explanation.correct: A management group can be deleted only when it has no child management groups and no subscriptions under it, and when the requester holds write permissions on the group (Owner, Contributor, or Management Group Contributor). The account in this scenario already has Contributor on contoso-sandbox, so the blocking condition is the content underneath. Moving the child management group and its subscriptions to another parent management group empties contoso-sandbox, after which the group itself can be removed.

perChoice.b: Deletion isn't cascading. A management group that still contains child management groups or subscriptions can't be deleted, and the portal makes this explicit: if the Delete button is unavailable, hovering over it shows the reason. Content underneath must be moved out first.
perChoice.c: Moving contoso-sandbox to a different parent management group changes where the group sits in the tree; it doesn't remove it, so contoso-sandbox still exists and still carries its children, and the goal of retiring the container isn't met.
perChoice.d: A Global Administrator role relates to elevating access to the root management group, and role assignments on that root apply to the whole directory. Removal of a management group isn't performed at the root level, and elevation there gives no shortcut past the requirement that the group be empty before deletion.

body.stem: A new team needs read-only visibility across everything the company runs in Azure. You want to grant the Reader role once, on the contoso-corp management group, so the access reaches every subscription and resource underneath it. Which value should be passed to the -Scope parameter of New-AzRoleAssignment?

options.text: /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/contoso-corp
/subscriptions/contoso-corp
/providers/Microsoft.Management/subscriptions/contoso-corp
/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/sub-prod-01

explanation.correct: When you target a management group from a resource provider's actions such as a role assignment, the scope path is /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{yourMgID}, for example New-AzRoleAssignment -Scope "/providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/Contoso". Any Azure role assigned at a management group inherits down the hierarchy, so an assignment made on contoso-corp reaches the subscriptions beneath it and the resources inside them.

perChoice.b: A path of the form /subscriptions/{id} addresses a subscription, not a management group, and contoso-corp is a group identifier rather than a subscription ID. The assignment wouldn't attach to the management group.
perChoice.c: The resource path segment for a management group is managementGroups, not subscriptions. Microsoft.Management/subscriptions doesn't address the management group container, so the assignment can't be created on contoso-corp.
perChoice.d: The path shape is right, but sub-prod-01 is the identifier of a subscription in the hierarchy, not of a management group. The command therefore doesn't resolve the container you intend to govern.

body.stem: Your platform team runs routine hierarchy work through the Azure CLI on the company's tenant. Match each requested change to the command that performs it.

slots.label: Place an existing subscription inside a group so that group's settings apply to it
Take a subscription out of the group it currently belongs to
Nest an existing management group under a different container in the tree
Print a group together with every level that sits beneath it
Erase a container that no longer has anything under it

explanation.correct: Each command maps to the change described: the subscription subcommands add and remove tie a subscription to or untie it from a group, the update command with a parent value re-parents a management group, show with the expand and recurse flags returns the group plus every level under it, and delete removes a group.

perChoice.i1: This is the command that attaches an existing subscription to a group, which is what 'place an existing subscription inside a group' asks for; once there, the subscription inherits the access and policies defined on that group.
perChoice.i2: This drops the link between the subscription and the group named by --name, which is what 'take a subscription out of the group it currently belongs to' requires.
perChoice.i3: The update command combined with a parent value moves an existing management group so it sits under another one; this is the documented way to re-parent a group.
perChoice.i4: The show command returns a single group's information, and adding the expand and recurse flags includes all levels of the hierarchy beneath it, matching the 'print every level' request.
perChoice.i5: The delete command removes the management group named by --name; it only works when nothing is nested under the group and when you hold write permissions on it.

body.stem: A platform engineer is building Azure role definitions and role assignments for a management group hierarchy. Match each reported case to the guidance that resolves it.

rows: The scope field holds "Contoso Corporate" instead of the container key.
A brand-new role lists contoso-sandbox and contoso-sandbox-we in its assignable scopes.
The role carries a section for data-plane operations and the team wants to grant it on a group.
The scope key contso-sandbx (one letter missing) is saved with no error.
A runbook identity must start and stop virtual machines everywhere below a container.

items.text: Use the full path /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{groupId} rather than the portal label.
Split the entry: a new role definition may list a single management group only.
Assign that definition further down instead; it can't be granted at this scope.
Nothing fails at creation time, so the problem only surfaces when the role is attached.
Put the VM Contributor role on the container; it reaches every machine below and cannot reshape the container.

slots.label: Case A
Case B
Case C
Case D
Case E

explanation.correct: A management group is referenced in a custom role definition by its identifier in the full path /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{groupId}, not by the display name (Case A). A new role definition may contain only one management group in its assignable scopes (Case B). Custom roles with DataActions can't be assigned at the management group scope, so the assignment must be made lower in the hierarchy (Case C). Azure Resource Manager doesn't validate that a management group named in the assignable scopes exists, so a typo is accepted at creation and only causes trouble later (Case D). For the runbook identity, assigning the built-in VM Contributor role on a management group gives access to all VMs underneath while the role itself performs no action on the management group (Case E).

perChoice.i1: Resolves Case A: the scope must use the management group's ID in the full path, and using the display name is the common error called out for custom role definitions.
perChoice.i2: Resolves Case B: only one management group can be defined in the assignable scopes of a new role, so the second group needs its own definition.
perChoice.i3: Resolves Case C: custom roles containing DataActions can't be assigned at the management group scope; assign them at a subscription or lower scope instead.
perChoice.i4: Resolves Case D: Azure Resource Manager doesn't validate the existence of the management group in the assignable scopes, so a mistyped key still produces a definition and only shows up when someone assigns the role.
perChoice.i5: Resolves Case E: VM Contributor assigned on a management group has no action on the management group itself but inherits down the hierarchy to every VM under it.

body.stem: A platform team is sizing a management group hierarchy for a new tenant and confirming how the tree can be shaped. Match each question they raised to what the service allows.

items.text: They must trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant.

slots.label: How many management groups can exist in one directory
How many parents a management group or subscription can have
Where a newly provisioned subscription lands before anyone reorganizes it
Membership rule for everything filed under one group

explanation.correct: A single directory can support 10,000 management groups; each management group and subscription supports only one parent; new subscriptions automatically default to the root management group when created; and all subscriptions within a single management group must trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant.

perChoice.i1: This answers the capacity question: a single directory supports 10,000 management groups.
perChoice.i2: This answers how many parents are allowed: each management group and each subscription can have only one parent.
perChoice.i3: This answers where a new subscription starts: new subscriptions automatically default to the root management group when they are created.
perChoice.i4: This answers the membership rule: all subscriptions within a single management group must trust the same Microsoft Entra tenant.

body.stem: A governance team is preparing its runbook for how Azure treats management groups during day-to-day operation. Match each situation to what actually happens.

items.text: It is placed under the root management group or the default one, and the creator gets an Owner assignment on it.
Setup runs behind the scenes for the hierarchy and can take up to 15 minutes before a notification arrives.
Hierarchy data is cached for up to 30 minutes; a fresh token makes the update visible sooner.
That group can't be moved or removed; only its display name can be changed, and that needs Owner or Contributor there.
Query Azure Monitor activity logs with the scope /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{id}.

slots.label: A signed-in tenant user opens the blade with no write permission on the top-level group and hierarchy protection off
A brand-new directory begins using this service for the first time
An engineer relocates a container and the portal still lists the old arrangement
A script attempts to relocate or delete the group sitting at the very top of the tree
Auditors must see who changed access and policies on a group from outside the portal

explanation.correct: Any Microsoft Entra ID user can create a management group without management group write permission when hierarchy protection isn't enabled; the new group becomes a child of the root or default management group and the creator is given an Owner role assignment (slot 1). The first management group in a directory can take up to 15 minutes to complete, with a notification when it's done (slot 2). Azure Resource Manager caches user tokens and management group hierarchy details for 30 minutes, and refreshing the token reveals updates sooner (slot 3). The root management group can't be moved or deleted; only its display name can be changed, which requires Owner or Contributor on it (slot 4). Management groups are supported in Azure Monitor activity logs, queried outside the portal at the scope /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{management-group-id} (slot 5).

perChoice.i1: This fits the situation where a user without write permission creates a group while hierarchy protection is off: the service allows it, places the group under the root or the default management group, and gives the creator an Owner role assignment.
perChoice.i2: This fits the initial setup of a directory: the first management group created can take up to 15 minutes to complete while processes set the service up, and a notification is sent when the process finishes.
perChoice.i3: This fits the stale portal view after a hierarchy change: Azure Resource Manager caches management group hierarchy details and user tokens for 30 minutes, and refreshing the browser, signing in and out, or requesting a new token reveals the update sooner.
perChoice.i4: This fits the attempt to relocate or delete the top-level group: the root management group can't be moved or deleted, and to change its display name your account must have the Owner or Contributor role on it.
perChoice.i5: This fits the audit requirement: management groups are supported in Azure Monitor activity logs, and outside the portal the target scope is /providers/Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/{management-group-id}.

body.stem: A platform engineer automates management group administration with Azure PowerShell cmdlets. Match each cmdlet parameter to what the team needs it to do.

slots.label: Identifies which container the cmdlet acts on, using the value that is fixed once the container exists
Sets the label that people see for the container in the portal
Nests an existing container under a different container in the tree
Names the Azure billing scope that should be tied to or untied from a container
Returns the container together with every level nested beneath it

explanation.correct: The AzManagementGroup cmdlets take -GroupId (an alias of -GroupName) as the identifier of the management group a command targets, and that identifier can't be edited after creation (slot 1). Update-AzManagementGroup -DisplayName changes only the label shown in the portal, which can be changed at any time (slot 2). Update-AzManagementGroup with -ParentId moves a management group under a different one (slot 3). New-AzManagementGroupSubscription and Remove-AzManagementGroupSubscription use -SubscriptionId to name the subscription being attached to or detached from a group (slot 4). Get-AzManagementGroup with -Expand and -Recurse returns a group plus all the levels beneath it (slot 5).

perChoice.i1: Belongs in the first slot: -GroupId (aliased to -GroupName) supplies the management group ID that a cmdlet acts on, and that ID is the unique, non-editable identifier used throughout Azure.
perChoice.i2: Belongs in the second slot: -DisplayName sets the display name, which is the separate label shown in the portal and can be changed at any time.
perChoice.i3: Belongs in the third slot: passing -ParentId to Update-AzManagementGroup moves the group under another group, as in Update-AzManagementGroup -GroupId 'Contoso' -ParentId $parentGroup.id.
perChoice.i4: Belongs in the fourth slot: -SubscriptionId names the subscription that New-AzManagementGroupSubscription attaches to a group or that Remove-AzManagementGroupSubscription detaches from it.
perChoice.i5: Belongs in the fifth slot: combining -Expand and -Recurse on Get-AzManagementGroup returns the requested group and all levels of the hierarchy under it.

body.stem: You have a directory with many Azure subscriptions and a governance rollout that has to cover the hierarchy, the role assignments made on it, and Azure Policy. Five teams each need one narrow capability, and the plan is to give each team a single built-in role at the management group level. Match each team's requirement to the role you should assign.

slots.label: Add, rename, move and delete containers, attach policy and grant role assignments, with these rights applying at this one level only and not to the subscriptions beneath
Control containers, policy and role assignments at this scope, with the rights inherited by the subscriptions and resources underneath
Issue and withdraw role assignments for other principals, with no other powers over the hierarchy
See this single container in the portal and nothing beneath it, with no ability to make changes
See this container, the containers nested inside it, the subscriptions and the resources in them, with no ability to make changes

explanation.correct: The five requirements map onto the built-in roles the documentation lists as usable at a management group. The team that must reshape the hierarchy but only at that one level gets Management Group Contributor, because the chart marks create, rename, move, delete, assign access and assign policy as supported and notes that this role performs those actions only at the management group scope. The team that needs those rights to flow down to the subscriptions and resources underneath gets Owner, which is supported for every action and is not limited to the single scope, and permissions assigned on a management group are inherited by its descendants. The team that only hands out and withdraws role assignments gets User Access Administrator, the one action listed for it being assign access. The two viewing teams split because Management Group Reader is marked as acting only at the management group scope, while Reader is simply a read role whose permissions are inherited by everything below.

perChoice.mgc: Fits the team that adds, renames, moves and deletes containers and handles both policy and role assignments at that one level: the chart shows create, rename, move, delete, assign access and assign policy as supported, and the documentation notes this role performs those actions only at the management group scope, so nothing flows down to the subscriptions beneath.
perChoice.own: Fits the team whose rights must be inherited by the subscriptions and resources underneath: the chart shows a check mark for every action, and unlike Management Group Contributor and Management Group Reader this role isn't limited to the management group scope, so child resources inherit the permissions.
perChoice.rdr: Fits the team that must see the whole branch below the assignment: Reader supports read, and because permissions assigned on a management group are inherited by the resources in the hierarchy, the subscriptions and resources underneath are visible as well.
perChoice.mgr: Fits the team that sees only the single container it was assigned on: the chart gives this role read only, and the documentation notes it performs the allowed action only at the management group scope, so nothing nested beneath becomes visible.
perChoice.uaa: Fits the team whose entire job is issuing and withdrawing role assignments for other principals: assign access is the only supported action for this role, and it grants no powers over the hierarchy itself.

body.stem: Your tenant contains 420 Azure subscriptions, and every one of them sits directly beneath the directory's single top-level container. A security rule must block virtual machine creation in two regions across all of them, and it must also cover subscriptions the company adds next year. You need one assignment, made in a scope that new subscriptions inherit automatically. Which management group should you assign the policy to?

rows: Virtual machine creation blocked in eastus and northeurope
420, each a direct child of the directory's single top-level container
Automatically placed under that same top-level container

body.statement: You should assign the policy at the {{scope}} so that every subscription inherits it.

options.text: The root management group
Each subscription that hosts virtual machines
A separate management group per blocked region
The management group that holds the company's landing zones

explanation.correct: Every directory has one built-in top-level management group, and all other management groups and subscriptions fold up to it. Anything assigned there - policies, role assignments - cascades by inheritance to the whole tree, and new subscriptions are placed under it automatically, so a single assignment covers today's subscriptions and any created later.

perChoice.scope:b: An assignment made on a subscription applies only to that subscription, so the rule would have to be repeated 420 times and each future subscription would need its own copy.
perChoice.scope:c: A new group per blocked region only covers the subscriptions placed beneath it, and placing subscriptions under those groups changes the governance hierarchy rather than covering everything at once.
perChoice.scope:d: A group that holds only the landing zones covers just its own descendants, so subscriptions elsewhere in the directory, including future ones created at the top, would not inherit the rule.

body.stem: In your Microsoft Entra directory, nobody holds a role on the single top-level management group, so no one can currently be given rights anywhere in the hierarchy. A member of the Microsoft Entra Global Administrators role has been asked to open that group and hand out role assignments to colleagues so they can shape the hierarchy. Which step must be taken first?
body.statement: The Global Administrator must {{step}} before role assignments can be made on that group.

options.text: Elevate access, then assign roles from that group
Assign the Owner role on that group first
Assign the Management Group Contributor role on that group first
Create a child management group and assign roles there instead

explanation.correct: No one has permissions on the root management group by default, and Microsoft Entra Global Administrators are the only identities that can obtain them. They do this by elevating their access, which grants them the User Access Administrator role on the root management group; only then can they assign any Azure role to other users or groups to manage the hierarchy.

perChoice.step:b: Owner is just another role, and it cannot be self-assigned on the root management group because the person has no permissions there yet. The permission has to come from elevating access first.
perChoice.step:c: Management Group Contributor is also only a role that can be granted after the person already holds permissions on that group, so assigning it is a result of the first step rather than the first step itself.
perChoice.step:d: Creating a child group and assigning roles there does nothing for the top-level group itself; the request here is about the directory-wide group, and access to it can only be obtained by elevating access.

body.stem: A platform team wants a single view that lists every networking resource in the tenant, even though those resources sit in many different subscriptions and resource groups, and the team must not change how policies or role assignments inherit down the hierarchy. The same resource must be able to appear in several of these views at the same time. Which type of container should the team create?

rows: Networking resources sit in 40 subscriptions and 300 resource groups
Policy and role assignments are already in place and must keep inheriting as before
A resource in more than one view
Team, project and environment views over the same resources
Viewers must see the view without being able to change the resources in it

body.statement: The team should create {{container}} for that view.

options.text: Service groups
Management groups
Resource groups
Azure tags

explanation.correct: Service groups are created at tenant level in the Microsoft.Management resource provider and let resources, resource groups and subscriptions from anywhere in the hierarchy be connected into a single group without reorganizing the existing hierarchy. A resource can belong to several groups at once, which supports the team, project and environment views, and permissions on a service group don't grant access to the resources it contains, which keeps the team on least privilege.

perChoice.container:b: Management groups build the governance hierarchy above subscriptions so that access and policies inherit downward. They are not a grouping for resources shared across scope boundaries, and every subscription can have only one parent.
perChoice.container:c: Resource groups exist inside a single subscription and are used for the deployment and lifecycle of closely related resources, so they can't span the 40 subscriptions in this scenario.
perChoice.container:d: Tags are metadata added to individual resources. They can be used as criteria in policy, but they don't create a container, don't aggregate resources into a view and carry no permission inheritance.

body.stem: A move of subscription sub-retail-01 out of contoso-sales and into contoso-eu was rejected this morning. Your role assignments on the three scopes involved are listed below. Which change would allow the move to succeed?
body.statement: To allow the move, you should {{change}}.

options.text: Grant a role that includes Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/write on contoso-sales
Grant a role that includes Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write on contoso-eu
Grant a role that includes Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/subscriptions/write on contoso-sales
Grant a role that includes Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/write on contoso-eu

explanation.correct: A move is evaluated at three layers: the child subscription being moved, the target parent management group and the current parent management group. Each layer needs Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/write. Owner already gives you that on sub-retail-01 and on contoso-eu, but Reader on contoso-sales only reads, so write on the current parent is the missing piece.

perChoice.change:b: Owner on contoso-eu already includes Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write, and extra role assignment rights on the target parent aren't what's missing.
perChoice.change:c: Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/subscriptions/write is required on the child subscription, where you already hold Owner. Granting it on the current parent doesn't satisfy the current-parent requirement, which is Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/write.
perChoice.change:d: Owner on contoso-eu already includes Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/write, so granting it again on that scope changes nothing.

body.stem: Your security team must review every role assignment and policy assignment change recorded against contoso-corp in one place, including changes made outside the Azure portal, and must forward those records to their long-term monitoring platform for retention. Which approach should they configure?

rows: Role assignment and policy assignment events recorded against contoso-corp
Include events raised outside the portal
Automation, template deployments and CLI activity
Records must be kept for 400 days for compliance
Only contoso-corp is in scope, not the rest of the tenant

options.text: Diagnostic settings that route its activity log entries to Log Analytics
A policy assignment that audits resources in every subscription beneath it
A role assignment that gives the security team the Monitoring Reader role on it
A scheduled Get-AzManagementGroup -GroupId contoso-corp script that exports the hierarchy

explanation.correct: Management groups are supported in Azure Monitor activity logs, so events such as role assignment and policy assignment changes made to contoso-corp can be queried in the same central place as other Azure resources, whether the change came from the portal or from automation. Using the Azure Resource Manager REST API, diagnostic settings can be enabled on the management group to send those activity log entries to a Log Analytics workspace, Azure Storage or Azure Event Hubs, which satisfies the retention requirement.

perChoice.approach:b: A policy assignment defines the allowed or denied state of resources and doesn't capture a stream of historical events, so it can't satisfy a review or retention requirement.
perChoice.approach:c: A role assignment only grants permissions. The Monitoring Reader role lets a team query monitoring data but creates no forwarding of that scope's records to another system.
perChoice.approach:d: Get-AzManagementGroup returns the management group object and its hierarchy as it stands at the time it runs. It doesn't return the history of changes, and nothing forwards those records anywhere.

body.stem: You have a Microsoft Entra directory in which hierarchy protection isn't enabled. A new employee must create the management group that will hold the pilot landing zone subscriptions, and you don't want to hand that person any permission ahead of time. Which statement is accurate?

columns: Direct role assignments in the directory

body.statement: When nora@contoso.com creates that management group, {{outcome}}.

options.text: no permission check blocks the request, and the creator receives an Owner role assignment
the request is blocked until a Global Administrator elevates that person's access to the root management group
no permission check blocks the request, and the creator receives a Reader role assignment
no permission check blocks the request, and the creator receives a Management Group Contributor role assignment

explanation.correct: With hierarchy protection not enabled, any user in the tenant can create a management group without already holding management group write permission. The new group is placed under the root management group (or the default management group), and the service automatically gives the creator an Owner role assignment on it, so no permission has to be granted beforehand.

perChoice.outcome:b: Elevating access at the root management group is what a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator does so they can start assigning roles to other people; it isn't a prerequisite for a user with no permissions to create a management group when hierarchy protection is off.
perChoice.outcome:c: The role assignment the service creates for the account that creates the group is Owner, which grants full control over the new group. Reader is read-only and gives the person nothing they can administer with.
perChoice.outcome:d: Management Group Contributor permits creating, renaming and deleting child management groups, but it isn't the role the service grants automatically to the account that creates a management group.
